title: Transformers

notes.heading: 1. Mutual Induction Principle, EMF Equation & Constant-Flux Operation
notes.proseLatex: A transformer is a STATIC electromagnetic device transferring AC power between circuits at CONSTANT FREQUENCY! Never apply pure DC to a transformer primary — since $d\Phi/dt = 0$, zero back-EMF is induced and low winding resistance $R_1$ causes primary burnout! Sinusoidal core flux $\Phi(t) = \Phi_m\sin(2\pi f t)$ induces RMS EMFs $E_1 = 4.44\,f N_1 \Phi_m$ and $E_2 = 4.44\,f N_2 \Phi_m$ (where $4.44 = \sqrt{2}\pi = 4\times 1.11$ incorporates the sinusoidal form factor $1.11$). Notice $\Phi_m \propto V_1/f$: keeping $V_1/f$ constant holds core flux density $B_m$ constant!

keyFormulas.label: Transformer RMS EMF Equation & Ideal Turns Ratio
keyFormulas.latex: $E = 4.44\,f N \Phi_m = 4.44\,f N B_m A_c,\qquad \frac{E_2}{E_1} = \frac{N_2}{N_1} = \frac{I_1}{I_2},\qquad Z_1' = \left(\frac{N_1}{N_2}\right)^2 Z_2$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Compute core flux/turns and refer impedances across transformer windings via (N1/N2)^2.

examples.problemLatex: A $2200/220\text{ V},\; 50\text{ Hz}$ transformer has $N_2 = 55$ secondary turns. Find $N_1$ and peak core flux $\Phi_m$.

notes.heading: 2. Core vs Copper Losses, Silicon-Steel Laminations & OC/SC Tests
notes.proseLatex: Core (iron) loss $P_i = P_h + P_e$ stays essentially CONSTANT from no-load to full-load (measured by Open-Circuit test at rated voltage on the LV side!): hysteresis loss $P_h \propto B_m^{1.6} f$ is minimized using high-silicon CRGO steel ($3\text{--}4\%\text{ Si}$), and eddy-current loss $P_e \propto B_m^2 f^2 t^2$ is minimized using thin insulated laminations ($0.35\text{--}0.5\text{ mm}$). Ohmic copper loss $P_{\text{cu}} = x^2 P_{\text{cu,fl}}$ varies as the SQUARE of fractional kVA load $x$ (measured by Short-Circuit test at rated current on the HV side!).

keyFormulas.label: Hysteresis/Eddy Scaling & OC/SC Test Summary
keyFormulas.latex: $P_h \propto B_m^{1.6} f,\quad P_e \propto B_m^2 f^2 t^2,\quad \text{OC test} \to P_i,\qquad \text{SC test (rated }I\text{)} \to P_{\text{cu,fl}}$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Match laminations vs silicon steel to eddy vs hysteresis losses and interpret OC/SC wattmeter readings.

notes.heading: 3. Efficiency, Maximum-Efficiency Criterion & Voltage Regulation
notes.proseLatex: Transformer kVA rating (not kW!) is specified because core loss depends on $V$ and copper loss depends on $I$, independent of load power factor $\cos\phi_2$. Efficiency at load fraction $x$ is $\eta = \frac{x S\cos\phi_2}{x S\cos\phi_2 + P_i + x^2 P_{\text{cu,fl}}}$, reaching MAXIMUM efficiency when variable copper loss equals constant iron loss ($x^2 P_{\text{cu,fl}} = P_i \implies x_{\eta\max} = \sqrt{P_i / P_{\text{cu,fl}}}$) and unity power factor ($\cos\phi_2 = 1$). Zero voltage regulation CAN occur only on a LEADING (capacitive) power factor load!

keyFormulas.label: Maximum-Efficiency Condition & Voltage Regulation
keyFormulas.latex: $\eta_{\max}\text{ at } x^2 P_{\text{cu,fl}} = P_i \implies S_{\eta\max} = S_{\text{rated}}\sqrt{\frac{P_i}{P_{\text{cu,fl}}}};\quad \text{VR} \approx I_2 R_{02}\cos\phi_2 \pm I_2 X_{02}\sin\phi_2$
keyFormulas.aiExplainContext: Calculate kVA for maximum efficiency and sign of voltage regulation (+/- for lag/lead).

examples.problemLatex: A $100\text{ kVA}$ transformer has core loss $P_i = 1\text{ kW}$ and full-load copper loss $P_{\text{cu,fl}} = 4\text{ kW}$. At what kVA load does maximum efficiency occur?

A $100\text{ kVA}$ transformer has core loss $P_i = 1\text{ kW}$ and full-load copper loss $P_{\text{cu,fl}} = 4\text{ kW}$. At what kVA load does maximum efficiency occur?

wbjeebTraps: Laminating the core reduces EDDY-CURRENT loss; adding silicon reduces HYSTERESIS loss — WBJEEB loves swapping these two!
At HALF load ($x = 0.5$), copper loss drops to ONE-FOURTH ($\frac{1}{4}P_{\text{cu,fl}}$), NOT half, while iron loss $P_i$ stays unchanged!
Transformers are rated in kVA (not kW), preserve frequency ($f_2 = f_1$), and burn out on DC primary excitation.
